MARCH 15, 2026

⭕️ BREAKING —

• Iran launches another ballistic missile attack on central Israel. One man in his 60s moderately injured after being struck by glass shards.

• Iran deploys the solid-fuel Sejjil ballistic missile for the first time in the conflict during the latest wave of attacks.

• Iranian-backed militia launches FPV drone strike near Victory Base by Baghdad Airport.

• Israel approves $826 million in emergency military procurement funding amid the ongoing war with Iran.

U.S. —

• U.S. bomber operations intensify from RAF Fairford, with 18 strategic bombers staged and multiple sorties launched in Operation Epic Fury.

• CENTCOM confirms continued B-52 strike missions over the region.

• The six U.S. service members killed in the KC-135 crash during the war have been publicly identified.

• Trump says the U.S. has identified shooters targeting protesters inside Iran and warned them to stand down.

ISRAEL —

• Israeli intelligence launches the “Quds file,” a campaign targeting Iran’s Quds Force infrastructure across the Middle East.

• Seven senior Quds Force officials reportedly killed in Lebanon and 17 of 20 Quds cargo aircraft destroyed, disrupting weapons transfers to proxies.

• IDF strikes IRGC drone storage facility in western Iran using real-time intelligence.

• Israeli Air Force footage shows Iranian soldiers fleeing drone facilities before follow-up strikes eliminate them.

• Israel’s foreign minister says the country does not lack interceptor missiles, pushing back on reports of shortages.

IRAN —

• Iranian leadership claims the latest strike wave, dubbed Operation True Promise wave 54, used Sejjil solid-fuel missiles.

• Iranian officials threaten to use control of the Strait of Hormuz as leverage against the United States and Israel.

• Israeli intelligence says Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is injured and in poor condition, while Iran claims he is healthy and directing operations.

• Internet access across Iran has been largely shut down for over two weeks, according to NetBlocks.

LEBANON —

• Hezbollah releases footage claiming a strike on a military industry site near Acre in northern Israel.

• Lebanese political figures call for detaining Iran’s ambassador and propose a peace-for-land initiative with Israel.

MIDDLE EAST —

• Bahrain says its air defenses have intercepted 125 missiles and 211 drones launched from Iran since the war began.

• Saudi Arabia intercepts 10 Iranian drones near Riyadh and eastern regions.

• Iranian missile and drone attacks target Israel, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait in coordinated waves.

• Smoke reported near Sheikh Isa Air Force Base in Bahrain following Iranian strike.

GLOBAL —

• Ukraine signals willingness to provide drone technology support in the Middle East conflict in exchange for funding and technology transfers.

• South Korea reviews U.S. requests for allied naval deployments to secure the Strait of Hormuz.

• Mount Kanlaon volcano erupts in the Philippines.

• Flooding damages homes and farmland in Waialua, Hawaii.

Nilahukan ito ng 73 Barangay GAD Focal Persons at VAW Desk Officers mula sa iba-ibang barangay sa lungsod. Layon ng aktibidad na mas mapalalim ang kanilang kaalaman at pagpapahalaga sa mahalagang papel ng kababaihan sa kasaysayan ng lungsod.

Kabilang sa binisita ang ilang makasaysayang lugar tulad ng Quezon Heritage House, Bahay Modernismo, Underparadiso, General Emilio Jacinto Monument, Tandang Sora Shrine, at Tandang Sora Women’s Museum.

Katuwang sa programa ang Quezon City Tourism Department, Quezon City Green Transport Office – Department of Public Order and Safety, at Traffic and Transport Management Department.

data.text:
Seventy-seven women saved thousands of lives under enemy fire, endured three years as prisoners of war, and returned to a country that forgot their names. They were the Angels of Bataan—but history treated them like ghosts.

In December 1941, just hours after the attack on Pearl Harbor, 66 Army nurses and 11 Navy nurses found themselves on the front lines of World War II in the Philippines. They weren’t meant to be there—military doctrine didn’t envision women in combat. But war doesn’t wait for policy.

As Manila fell to the Japanese, the nurses evacuated to the Bataan Peninsula, setting up field hospitals in the jungle. With no walls, only mosquito nets, and constant bombings overhead, they treated thousands of wounded soldiers. They worked grueling 20-hour shifts in suffocating heat, using limited supplies, and sterilizing bandages by boiling them. Despite the overwhelming conditions, they never stopped.

By April 1942, as Bataan collapsed, the nurses were evacuated to Corregidor, an island fortress. There, they set up their hospital underground in the Malinta Tunnel. It was dark, suffocating, and bombed daily. But they kept going, saving lives in any way they could, under constant threat of death.

On May 6, 1942, Corregidor fell. The nurses became prisoners of war—the largest group of American military women ever captured. They were transported to Manila and imprisoned in brutal camps, where they survived on starvation rations and faced rampant disease. Despite their own suffering, they continued to care for the sick, fashioning bamboo crutches and trading food for clean water to save others.

For nearly three years, the Angels of Bataan endured unimaginable hardship. They watched fellow prisoners die, but they never stopped helping. Then, in February 1945, American forces liberated them. The 66 Army nurses were freed, followed shortly by the 11 Navy nurses. Miraculously, all 77 women survived.

But when they returned home, the nation’s gratitude was lukewarm. The men received parades and front-page stories. The women received quiet commendations and were expected to move on, their suffering largely overlooked.

For decades, the Angels of Bataan were forgotten. Their heroic efforts were reduced to footnotes in history books, overshadowed by the stories of male soldiers. It wasn’t until the 1980s and 1990s that historians began to uncover their remarkable legacy. By then, many of the nurses had already passed away.

The Angels of Bataan proved that heroism doesn't always come with a weapon. It can come from refusing to abandon others, even when your own survival is in question. Seventy-seven women saved countless lives, and though history almost forgot them, their courage will never be erased.
